Responsibility Education Education and specialist qualifications are of key importance for Germany's future as a location for industry. STIHL is aware of its social responsibility and provides occupational training beyond its own needs. Under the guiding principle of sustainability, STIHL cooperates with schools and universities on long-term educational projects. The goal is to secure the supply of next-generation skilled workers and to prepare them for occupations requiring various qualifications. Training and further training STIHL has a long tradition of placing high priority on training. In order to facilitate entry into a successful career for as many young people as possible, we offer technical and commercial apprenticeships and also help to train our next-generation academics in collaboration with the Baden-Württemberg Cooperative State University. The goal is to provide optimal preparation for working in occupations requiring various qualifications and for a successful career at STIHL. Through various possibilities for further training, the company also gives all its employees the opportunity to continue developing their capabilities and strengths. Worldwide training Especially at the founding company in Germany, STIHL can look back on a long and successful tradition of occupational training. In recent years, established training concepts have been integrated also at STIHL sites where the local state school system does not foresee this type of training. In the United States for example, the training provided by STIHL Inc. offers many young people a unique opportunity to optimize their career prospects. And the STIHL plant in Brazil introduced occupational training according to the German system in 2013. Already in 2011, apprentice training courses were started at the STIHL plant in Qingdao, China, in cooperation with the Chamber of Foreign Trade. Educational partnerships STIHL actively supports school students in choosing a career, and helps them to develop their aptitudes and talents at an early stage. In Germany, this takes place for example through educational partnerships with state middle schools. Already in 2003, STIHL entered into a partnership with the school Friedensschule in Neustadt. This was the first cooperation of its kind in Baden-Württemberg. The cooperative ventures make school students acquainted with the diversity of working life through practical educational projects. They are also given specific orientation in searching for the right occupation. Klasse 2000 (Class 2000) "Strong and healthy at elementary school" is the motto of the Class 2000 teaching program, which is implemented throughout Germany by the Program Klasse 200 e.V. (Class 2000 Association). The children at the school Friedensschule in Neustadt for example learn what being healthy means by playing with Klaro, the program's mascot. STIHL helps and has supported the implementation of these lessons in elementary schools since 2007. Support for students' film concepts Each year, the Caligari Prize is awarded for the most innovative film concepts at the internationally renowned film academy in Ludwigsburg. STIHL has supported the students with the realization of their film ideas since 2006. Wolfgang Zahn, STIHL's Executive Board Member for Development, is involved as the Deputy Chairman of the Friends' Association of the Baden-Württemberg Film Academy. The award of the Caligari Prize constitutes valuable support for the winning students. It helps to integrate them in the Baden-Württemberg production landscape and thus also strengthens the Stuttgart region as a location for the media industry. Responsibility Employees At STIHL, corporate responsibility to our employees means that our workforce can count on us. Worldwide, almost 14,000 people work for STIHL. Sustainable and successful business operations are only possible through the joint efforts of the company's employees, management and owners. Social welfare and fair, cooperative teamwork have high priority at STIHL. A social approach STIHL has a tradition of granting voluntary social benefits that go far beyond what is agreed upon through collective bargaining. The basic principles of social welfare were already laid down by the company's founder, Andreas Stihl. The support fund that was established in 1939 was developed over the years into a modern company pension system. And for more than 40 years, there has also been a voluntary profit-sharing bonus. In addition, employees can acquire profit-participation rights, upon which interest is paid in relation to the company's earnings; in the past 20 years, this interest was usually at the maximum level of ten percent. When acquiring the profit-participation rights, the employees pay only one third of the price; the other two thirds are paid by the company. Job security Continuity in thoughts and actions is an important basis of our success. Ever since the company was founded, STIHL has always taken a long-term approach while maintaining flexibility and adaptability. This allows us to create secure jobs. In 2009, ANDREAS STIHL AG & Co. KG agreed with the General Employee Council on the continuation and further development of the company's own employment and site-guarantee agreement until December 31, 2020. Loyalty and solidarity Fair cooperation in a spirit of partnership with support from colleagues and open communication is a key element of our corporate culture. As a medium-sized family-owned business, we are particularly proud of the fact that our employees stay at STIHL for significantly longer than the industry average. One expression of this loyalty and solidarity is the tradition that employees' anniversaries at the company are honored by the Executive Board and the owning family and that the anniversaries are celebrated with the employees' families, colleagues and managers. Family and career It is not always easy to combine the needs of family and career. In order to meet the requirements of mothers and fathers at STIHL and to help them achieve a better balance between the working world and private life, we have implemented numerous measures. Together with the employees concerned, we arrange flexible working-time models that create scope for looking after children or other members of the family. Meanwhile, more than 120 models of working time exist which are tailored to operating and private needs. Through our family service, we also help employees to find suitable care facilities for their children or older family members. For example, places at a local childcare center are reserved for STIHL children. Safety at work Ensuring the safety of employees at work is a key task for STIHL. For this purpose, we have supplemented the statutory safety regulations with our own internal guidelines. STIHL employees and apprentices are trained in workshops and courses to avoid accidents at work at an early stage. STIHL's training department has developed the concept of an additional qualification as a "junior safety partner" together with the Wood and Metal Employers' Insurance Association. This concept has the objective of sensitizing and activating our workforce already as apprentices for issues such as occupational safety and protective equipment. Health care Protecting and promoting our employees' health is an important part of our social obligations. STIHL's health service offers professional medical care at work. The service's program includes medical examinations as well as the ergonomic design of workplaces, the provision of advice on health matters and the organization of Nordic walking and yoga courses. In addition, all sport enthusiasts can participate in a wide range of groups and courses in STIHL's company sport activities.

Responsibility Corporate responsibility has a long tradition at STIHL. As a medium-sized family-owned company, we believe we have a special obligation to society. We fulfill this obligation in many ways, for example with voluntary social benefits for our employees, with attractive apprenticeships and traineeships, and with social involvement close to our sites. Continuity and a long-term view guide our actions, and are part of our understanding of sustainability, just like resource-conserving production and the STIHL products with built-in environmental protection. The focal points of our social responsibility are in the areas of sustainable business operations, employees, the environment and education. The STIHL Group Leading the way for more than 90 years Our company founder Andreas Stihl developed his first chainsaw in 1926. His incentive: "To ease peoples' work with and in nature". This guiding principle is still of cardinal importance for us today. We design our products to match our customers' requirements. Since its foundation more than 90 years ago the company has grown from a one-man business into a global chainsaw and outdoor power equipment manufacturer. Innovative ideas, in-house know-how and meticulous craftsmanship have resulted in a broad and steadily expanding product portfolio. STIHL has been the world's biggest selling chainsaw brand since 1971. Our outstanding innovations have set the benchmark for the industry time and time again. We want to continue growing and maintaining our values in the future, too. After all, lasting success can only be achieved by adhering to solid principles. We are proud to look back on more than 90 years of STIHL. Learn more about our company and history here. Where can I purchase an iMow robotic mower? You can purchase the iMow robotic mower from selected STIHL dealers. You can find your nearest STIHL dealer at: http://www.stihl.com How can I adjust the cutting height? You can adjust the cutting height using the rotary knob on top of the iMow robotic mower. Select the desired cutting height with reference to the marking on the rotary knob. The minimum cutting height (setting 1) is 20 mm The maximum cutting height (setting 8) is 60 mm What happens to the clippings? The iMow robotic mower is a mulching mower. During mulching, the grass clippings are further shredded in the mowing deck housing after cutting. They then fall back into the turf, where they remain and decompose. The finely shredded clippings return organic nutrients to the lawn, serving as a natural fertiliser. Fertiliser requirements are thereby reduced significantly. How does the iMow robotic mower detect solid obstacles in the mowing area? The iMow robotic mower is equipped with a movable hood fitted with an impact sensor. If the iMow bumps into a solid obstacle (minimum height: 8 cm) in automatic mode, it stops, turns to face another direction and continues mowing. What are no-go areas? No-go areas are areas where the iMow robotic mower should not venture. No-go areas can include Ponds Swimming pools Flowerbeds Vegetable patches These areas must be cordoned off by routing the perimeter wire accordingly. What happens when the battery on the iMow robotic mower is completely discharged? The iMow robotic mower enters the docking station automatically at the end of the mowing operation or when the battery is low on energy. The number and duration of the mowing and charging operations within the active times are adapted fully automatically. What are guide loops for the offset drive home? Guide loops help the iMow identify corridors, confined areas and access points to the external docking station. If an external docking station and/or corridor has been installed in the mowing area, guide loops for the offset drive home must be provided. When the iMow robotic mower follows the perimeter wire offset at a distance, it crosses one of these guide loops during the drive home. It then travels to the perimeter wire and on to the docking station. What does the command "Start time-delayed mowing" mean? If the command "Start time-delayed mowing" is activated, the iMow robotic mower starts the mowing operation automatically after a time delay. The start and end times of the mowing operation must be defined. The mowing operation starts at the selected start time and continues until the selected end time. Is weather protection equipment available for the iMow robotic mower? A canopy top available as an accessory can be mounted on the docking station. This provides better protection for the iMow robotic mower against the weather. Where can I take my iMow robotic mower for servicing? Take your iMow robotic mower to a STIHL/VIKING dealer for servicing. When the annual service is due, a service message will appear on the display of the iMow. Will the iMow robotic mower also mow when it is raining? The iMow robotic mower can mow when it is raining. The rain sensor can be set so that the iMow robotic mower continues to operate normally when it is raining or mowing is interrupted or does not start when it is raining. How does the rain sensor function? The rain sensor can be set so that mowing is interrupted or does not start when it is raining. The current value is displayed in a line diagram in the menu under "SMART" > "Weather" > "Rain sensor". In order to set the 5-stage sensor, slide the control to the left or right. The rain sensor can also be set under "Settings" > "Rain sensor". The sensitivity of the rain sensor and the time the robotic mower waits for the sensor surface to dry following rain varies, depending on the setting. What happens if I forget my PIN? If you have forgotten your PIN and entered an incorrect PIN several times, you are prompted to enter the "master code". You can obtain this code from your STIHL/VIKING dealer. Can the iMow robotic mower mow lawn edges cleanly? Soft edges (ground level patios, paths, etc.) are positioned inside the perimeter wire in such a way that the mower produces perfectly clean results. Around hard edges such as walls, raised patios, etc., the iMow robotic mower is installed in such a way that it travels as close to the edge as possible, but always safely. What is the Anti-Stuck Manoeuvre (ASM)? When ASM is switched on, the iMow robotic mower starts an evasive routine if it gets stuck. On - Default setting Off - ASM should be switched off if: the mowing area contains larger level surfaces (e.g. asphalted drives) the robotic mower often turns 90° unexpectedly during the work the robotic mower remains stationary with the message 1131 without getting stuck during the work. What are the active times? During the active times, the iMow robotic mower is allowed to leave the docking station and mow the lawn. Mowing operations, charging operations and rest periods take place during these times. The iMow automatically distributes the mowing and charging operations between the available time windows. What is the dynamic mowing plan? The dynamic mowing plan enables the iMow to automatically complete the weekly mowing duration during the active times. This protects the lawn and ensures an optimal mowing result. Your iMow robotic mower's intelligence means that it can respond to external influences (cancellation due to rain, garden party, etc.) and distribute the mowing duration over other days. What is the automatic function? When automatic mowing is switched on, the iMow robotic mower independently leaves the docking station and mows the lawn during the active times. When automatic mowing is switched off, every mowing operation must be started manually. When should I replace the mowing blade? Replace the mowing blade at least every 200 operating hours. Where can I purchase a new mowing blade? You can purchase a new mowing blade from your nearest STIHL/VIKING dealer: Can I grind or re-sharpen the mowing blade? No, you should not grind or re-sharpen the mowing blade. How can I dispose of the iMow? Consult your recycling centre or your nearest STIHL/VIKING dealer for information on the proper disposal of waste products. The battery must be disposed of separately from the machine. Where can I purchase accessories for my iMow robotic mower? You can purchase accessories for your STIHL iMow robotic mower from your nearest STIHL/VIKING dealer. What should I do if a "Recommendation" appears in the status screen? The iMow robotic mower can still be operated, automatic operation continues. Recommendations are assigned the priority "Low" or "Info"; they appear in the status screen alternately with the text "iMow ready for op.". What should I do if a "Fault" occurs on the iMow robotic mower? Once you have acknowledged the fault on the display of your iMow robotic mower, the iMow can resume normal operation. Faults are assigned the priority "Medium" and require action by the user. What should I do if a "Error" message appears? If an error occur with the priority "High", the text "Contact your specialist dealer" appears on the display. The iMow robotic mower can only be operated again once the error has been rectified by a STIHL/VIKING specialist dealer. The iMow robotic mower does not enter the docking station automatically. What can I do? Possible causes: Uneven entry area to docking station Dirty drive wheels or dirty floor plate Perimeter wire incorrectly routed in area of docking station Ends of perimeter wire not cut Remedy: Level out the entry area to the docking station Clean the drive wheels and the floor plate of the docking station Re-route the perimeter wire - ensure correct routing in the area of the docking station Cut the perimeter wire as described and route it without excess length - do not roll up protruding ends The iMow robotic mower fails to mow when the "Start mowing" or "Start time-delayed mowing" commands are activated. What can I do? Possible cause: Insufficient battery charge Rain detected Flap not closed or not present Message is active Homecall activated on the docking station Charge the battery Setting the rain sensor Close the flap Rectify displayed fault and confirm the message with "OK" End Homecall or repeat command following docking The iMow robotic mower has crossed the perimeter wire. What can I do? Perimeter wire incorrectly routed, clearances are not correct Slope inclination of mowing area too steep Interference affecting the iMow robotic mower Check the routing of the perimeter wire, check clearances using the iMow Ruler Check the routing of the perimeter wire; block off areas with excessively steep slope inclinations Contact a STIHL/VIKING specialist dealer Impact sensor is not activated when the iMow robotic mower hits an obstacle. What can I do? Low obstacle (height less than 8 cm) The obstacle is not firmly attached to the ground Remove the obstacle or block it off with a no-go area The iMow robotic mower is not receiving any GPS signal. What can I do? The connection to the satellites is currently being established 3 or fewer satellites within range The machine is in a dead spot No further action required; it can take a few minutes to establish the connection Avoid or remove obstacles that might be blocking the signal (e.g. trees, canopies) Can I also use the iMow robotic mower to mow areas "manually"? You can mow areas "manually" using the RMI 632 models. The removable control panel allows you to operate the iMow robotic mower by hand both easily and conveniently. Is the iMow robotic mower fitted with an anti-theft alarm? The iMow robotic mower is fitted with an anti-theft alarm. When the anti-theft alarm is activated, an alarm signal sounds one minute after the robotic mower is lifted. This can be prevented or reversed by entering the PIN code. C models also offer GPS protection. When GPS protection is activated, the owner of the iMow robotic mower is notified by SMS and e-mail if the iMow is stolen from the home area. Which safety levels does the iMow robotic mower offer? The iMow robotic has 4 safety levels. Various locks and safety devices are activated, depending on the level: None: The iMow robotic mower is unprotected Low: Anti-theft alarm is active. A PIN code must be entered in order to link the iMow and docking station as well as reset the machine to the default settings. Medium: As "Low", but the time lock is also active. High: As "Medium", but settings can also only be changed following entry of the PIN code. Where can the docking station be positioned? Requirements for the docking station position: Protected, shady Level and even with the ground In the immediate vicinity of a suitable socket Free from sources of interference Metal, iron oxides and magnetic or electrically conductive materials as well as old perimeter wire installations can interfere with the mower's operation. It is recommended to remove these sources of interference. In order for docking to take place smoothly, no no-go areas must be installed within a radius of at least 2 m around the docking station. Floor plate: The docking station must not be inclined by more than 2 cm rearwards or 8 cm forwards. Never bend the ground plate. Any unevenness must be removed under the ground plate so that it fully contacts the ground. Can children remain within the mowing area during mowing operation? Children must be kept away from the iMow robotic mower and mowing area during mowing operation. Never allow the iMow robotic mower to operate if you know that animals or persons, particularly children, are in the vicinity. Never allow children to approach or play with the robotic mower. Can pets remain within the mowing area during mowing operation? Dogs and other pets must be kept away from the iMow robotic mower and mowing area during mowing operation. Never allow the iMow robotic mower to operate if you know that animals or persons, particularly children, are in the vicinity. With which mobile end devices is the iMow app compatible? The iMow app can be installed on a smartphone or tablet with iOS or Android operating system. An iMow web app for Internet browsers is also available. Visit the following page for more details: https://web.imow.stihl.com/systems Where can I download the latest version of the iMow app? You can download the latest version of the iMow app for end devices with an Android operating system from the Google Play Store . You can download the latest version of the iMow app for end devices with an iOS from the App Store How do I install the iMow app on my mobile end device? You can download the iMow app free of charge from the Google Play Store. You can download the iMow app free of charge from the App Store. In which languages is the iMow app available? The iMow app is available in 25 languages: Bulgarian, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hungarian, Italian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Russian, Serbian, Slovakian, Slovenian, Spanish, Sweden What are the system requirements of the iMow app? For an overview of the current system requirements for your end device, please visit: How does the login process work for the iMow app? After purchasing an iMow robotic mower model RMI 422 PC, RMI 632 C or RMI 632 PC, your specialist dealer will create a user account with your e-mail address. You will then receive a confirmation e-mail and can specify your password. You can use this information to log on to the iMow app. How much does it cost to use the app? Use of the iMow app and the mobile radio connection of the iMow robotic mower are included in the purchase price. The transmission of data will result in costs that must be borne by the user; these costs will be determined by the contract with the mobile phone provider or Internet provider. How can I reset my password? Select "Forgotten password" on the login page of the iMow app. Specify the e-mail address you used to register. You will receive an e-mail containing all other information and action steps. Alternatively, you can change your password via the account settings (My data - Password). What does STIHL do with my data? STIHL will only use your personal data, in particular machine, device and usage data, to fulfil your existing contract and for the purpose of providing you with product support. We also use this data to generate anonymous statistics, which we then use to improve our products and services, monitor our products and guarantee maximum product safety. Where can I manage my profile? Open the iMow app and select your profile picture or the round iMow symbol above your e-mail address to manage your profile. How can I set the mowing duration in the iMow app? To set the mowing duration in the iMow app, first select your iMow model in the overview. Then select "Smart" and then "Mowing duration". Here, you can adapt the time according to growth or change the mowing duration manually. What is my telephone number used for? Your telephone number is used to send you a message notifying you that the GPS anti-theft alarm has triggered. The telephone number is optional. What does it mean when "iMow is offline" is displayed in my iMow app? If "iMow is offline" appears in the iMow app, this means that the iMow robotic mower is currently not connected to the Internet. This could be for several reasons: the iMow has developed a fault the iMow has gone offline to save energy the iMow is located in a dead zone What is the average volume of data that the iMow robotic mower exchanges during regular operation (incoming and outgoing data)? An iMow consumes approx. 1 MB of data per month, depending on usage behaviour. Which mobile network does the iMow robotic mower select? The iMow robotic mower selects the strongest available 2G mobile network, so long as your local mobile phone provider is the same as one of our providers: https://www.viking-garden.com/roaming-provider.aspx What is the usual time delay after inputting a command in the iMow app? The technical processing time under ideal conditions is 1 second. The actual time delay depends on a number of factors such as the signal strength of the mobile radio connection of the iMow (GPRS reception), signal strength of the mobile network connection of the smartphone/tablet/PC, speed of the smartphone/tablet/PC, etc. Which type of data connection does the iMow robotic mower support? European iMow robotic mowers currently support 2G data connections. Which providers can the iMow use to establish a mobile radio connection? The iMow can use the following providers to establish a mobile radio connection: I do not receive any push notifications from the iMow app. Why is that? Check: whether the "Notification" function is activated in the account settings of the iMow app. whether you have configured your smartphone notification settings to receive iMow app push notifications. If you still do not receive push notifications, please contact the iMow support team at imowsupport@stihl.at How can I set the active times? You can set the active times directly using the "Mowing plan" menu item in the iMow display or under "Active times" in the iMow app. What is a desired zone? A desired zone is an area in the mowing area that is defined using the smartphone or tablet. The centre point of the desired zone is defined using the GPS receiver of the mobile phone and a radius around this coordinate is defined. The iMow robotic mower travels along the perimeter wire to the desired zone and mows the grass there. The radius selected must be large enough that the desired zone and perimeter wire overlap. You define the desired zone by clicking on the "+" symbol. A desired zone is only active once for the desired mowing duration. How is the current weather forecast taken into consideration? If the weather forecast is activated, the iMow robotic mower will take the forecasted weather into consideration within the active times. If rain is forecast for the end of the week, for example, the mowing times of the iMow robotic mower are postponed to the start of the week, if possible. If my iMow robotic mower encounters problems, will I receive a notification via the iMow app? Messages that affect normal operation are also reported to the iMow app. After the message is sent, the robotic mower switches to standby and the mobile radio connection is disabled (offline) to preserve the battery. What is GPS protection? The iMow robotic mower is fitted with a GPS receiver. When GPS protection is activated, the owner of the machine is notified if the machine is operated outside the home area via SMS and e-mail. The PIN code is also requested on the display. We recommend always activating the GPS protection.

Responsibility Education Education and specialist qualifications are of key importance for Germany's future as a location for industry. STIHL is aware of its social responsibility and provides occupational training beyond its own needs. Under the guiding principle of sustainability, STIHL cooperates with schools and universities on long-term educational projects. The goal is to secure the supply of next-generation skilled workers and to prepare them for occupations requiring various qualifications. Training and further training STIHL has a long tradition of placing high priority on training. In order to facilitate entry into a successful career for as many young people as possible, we offer technical and commercial apprenticeships and also help to train our next-generation academics in collaboration with the Baden-Württemberg Cooperative State University. The goal is to provide optimal preparation for working in occupations requiring various qualifications and for a successful career at STIHL. Through various possibilities for further training, the company also gives all its employees the opportunity to continue developing their capabilities and strengths. Worldwide training Especially at the founding company in Germany, STIHL can look back on a long and successful tradition of occupational training. In recent years, established training concepts have been integrated also at STIHL sites where the local state school system does not foresee this type of training. In the United States for example, the training provided by STIHL Inc. offers many young people a unique opportunity to optimize their career prospects. And the STIHL plant in Brazil introduced occupational training according to the German system in 2013. Already in 2011, apprentice training courses were started at the STIHL plant in Qingdao, China, in cooperation with the Chamber of Foreign Trade. Educational partnerships STIHL actively supports school students in choosing a career, and helps them to develop their aptitudes and talents at an early stage. In Germany, this takes place for example through educational partnerships with state middle schools. Already in 2003, STIHL entered into a partnership with the school Friedensschule in Neustadt. This was the first cooperation of its kind in Baden-Württemberg. The cooperative ventures make school students acquainted with the diversity of working life through practical educational projects. They are also given specific orientation in searching for the right occupation. Klasse 2000 (Class 2000) "Strong and healthy at elementary school" is the motto of the Class 2000 teaching program, which is implemented throughout Germany by the Program Klasse 200 e.V. (Class 2000 Association). The children at the school Friedensschule in Neustadt for example learn what being healthy means by playing with Klaro, the program's mascot. STIHL helps and has supported the implementation of these lessons in elementary schools since 2007. Support for students' film concepts Each year, the Caligari Prize is awarded for the most innovative film concepts at the internationally renowned film academy in Ludwigsburg. STIHL has supported the students with the realization of their film ideas since 2006. Wolfgang Zahn, STIHL's Executive Board Member for Development, is involved as the Deputy Chairman of the Friends' Association of the Baden-Württemberg Film Academy. The award of the Caligari Prize constitutes valuable support for the winning students. It helps to integrate them in the Baden-Württemberg production landscape and thus also strengthens the Stuttgart region as a location for the media industry. Responsibility Employees At STIHL, corporate responsibility to our employees means that our workforce can count on us. Worldwide, almost 14,000 people work for STIHL. Sustainable and successful business operations are only possible through the joint efforts of the company's employees, management and owners. Social welfare and fair, cooperative teamwork have high priority at STIHL. A social approach STIHL has a tradition of granting voluntary social benefits that go far beyond what is agreed upon through collective bargaining. The basic principles of social welfare were already laid down by the company's founder, Andreas Stihl. The support fund that was established in 1939 was developed over the years into a modern company pension system. And for more than 40 years, there has also been a voluntary profit-sharing bonus. In addition, employees can acquire profit-participation rights, upon which interest is paid in relation to the company's earnings; in the past 20 years, this interest was usually at the maximum level of ten percent. When acquiring the profit-participation rights, the employees pay only one third of the price; the other two thirds are paid by the company. Job security Continuity in thoughts and actions is an important basis of our success. Ever since the company was founded, STIHL has always taken a long-term approach while maintaining flexibility and adaptability. This allows us to create secure jobs. In 2009, ANDREAS STIHL AG & Co. KG agreed with the General Employee Council on the continuation and further development of the company's own employment and site-guarantee agreement until December 31, 2020. Loyalty and solidarity Fair cooperation in a spirit of partnership with support from colleagues and open communication is a key element of our corporate culture. As a medium-sized family-owned business, we are particularly proud of the fact that our employees stay at STIHL for significantly longer than the industry average. One expression of this loyalty and solidarity is the tradition that employees' anniversaries at the company are honored by the Executive Board and the owning family and that the anniversaries are celebrated with the employees' families, colleagues and managers. Family and career It is not always easy to combine the needs of family and career. In order to meet the requirements of mothers and fathers at STIHL and to help them achieve a better balance between the working world and private life, we have implemented numerous measures. Together with the employees concerned, we arrange flexible working-time models that create scope for looking after children or other members of the family. Meanwhile, more than 120 models of working time exist which are tailored to operating and private needs. Through our family service, we also help employees to find suitable care facilities for their children or older family members. For example, places at a local childcare center are reserved for STIHL children. Safety at work Ensuring the safety of employees at work is a key task for STIHL. For this purpose, we have supplemented the statutory safety regulations with our own internal guidelines. STIHL employees and apprentices are trained in workshops and courses to avoid accidents at work at an early stage. STIHL's training department has developed the concept of an additional qualification as a "junior safety partner" together with the Wood and Metal Employers' Insurance Association. This concept has the objective of sensitizing and activating our workforce already as apprentices for issues such as occupational safety and protective equipment. Health care Protecting and promoting our employees' health is an important part of our social obligations. STIHL's health service offers professional medical care at work. The service's program includes medical examinations as well as the ergonomic design of workplaces, the provision of advice on health matters and the organization of Nordic walking and yoga courses. In addition, all sport enthusiasts can participate in a wide range of groups and courses in STIHL's company sport activities.

Responsibility Society At STIHL we are firmly convinced that companies have a special responsibility to society. We gladly accept this responsibility – not only at our founding company in Waiblingen but also at our national and international subsidiaries. By initiating and supporting social and cultural projects we make a contribution to a positive development of society. SOS-Kinderdorf e.V. (SOS Children's Villages) STIHL supports SOS-Kinderdorf e.V. Over the past few years the STIHL workforce has been engaged in a number of fund-raising campaigns in aid of SOS children's villages in crisis regions. We support this involvement and top up the amounts collected. Furthermore, STIHL is directly involved on the spot in Germany. STIHL staff help to look after the grounds in SOS children's villages. The sponsoring partnership of our subsidiary VIKING and SOS children's villages in Austria has existed since 2004. In the last few years VIKING has campaigned for different SOS children's villages in Austria as well as other countries. In addition, the company supports children's villages throughout Austria with donations in kind. Young Trainees in Rio de Janeiro‘s Botanical Garden Rio de Janeiro's botanical garden is one of the most important of its kind in the world. The 200-year-old Jardim Bontânico do Rio de Janeiro, as it is called in Portuguese, offers a habitat for several thousand species, some of which are threatened. Cooperating with the Botanical Garden Research Institute, the Rio de Janeiro State Court and the Friends of the Botanical Garden Society, STIHL Brazil supports the Pró-Florescer project. In Pró-Florescer, 70 young people from socially disadvantaged backgrounds are trained as park guides, gardeners or administrative assistants. During their training, the young adults are given free board and lodging and clothing. In addition, they receive pocket money. Apart from acquiring technical know-how, the participants develop their community spirit, initiative and self-confidence. A team of specialists, teachers and psychologists accompany the training and assist the freshly trained young men and women in finding a job. The botanical garden also profits from Pró-Florescer: It has 70 additional workers – equipped with STIHL products. STIHL Brazil has been involved as a project partner since the early nineties. STIHL sponsors ten training places every year and supports the project with numerous donations, such as cordless electric products and personal protective equipment. Africa is coming New prospects for sustainable co-operation Since 2015, STIHL has been supporting the "Afrika kommt!" project in which young executive staff from the African sub-Sahara region comes to Germany for a year to do a nine-month internship in a German partner company in addition to a three-month language course. A mentor accompanies the trainee throughout this period. Participants in the program acquire an insight into German work processes and management methods. At the same time, the initiative is to serve as a foundation stone for sustainable economic co-operation with Africa and help create an international network. The Deutsche Gesellschaft für internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) is responsible for the organisation and implementation of the project. STIHL sees great potential in this project because the young African executives bring new ways of thinking and new outlooks with them. The company continues to maintain contact with its former trainees and appreciates the cultural and professional exchange. Together we are strong Sport brings people together – it was with this thought in mind that the Special Olympics Germany was founded in 1991. The aim is to inspire mentally and physically impaired people to take part in sports and, at the same time, give them the opportunity to participate in the life of society. The purpose is not only to win medals, but to convey the joy of living and the fun of sports and thus improve independence and the quality of life. STIHL has been supporting the Special Olympics State Association in Rhineland-Palatinate since 2006, for social inclusion is a subject very close to STIHL‘s heart. Working together with Special Olympics, we want to strengthen the acceptance of people with disabilities. At the state games, about 1,300 athletes compete in 14 events and show that sport can transcend borders and bring down barriers. Schule meets High School Overcoming language barriers and finding new friends There has been a student exchange program between the Staufer Grammar School in Waiblingen and Tallwood High School in Virginia Beach since 2012. STIHL and its US subsidiary STIHL Inc. made a significant contribution to establishing the program. This is now an annual event on the calendar. Waiblingen students get to know the life of an American high school student for two weeks. They live with an American family, attend school with their American counterparts and go on excursions in the area. A few months later the young students from Virginia Beach come to stay with the families of the German students. The participants are invited to visit the local STIHL plant in both America and Germany. STIHL and STIHL Inc. support the exchange program financially, too. Rems Valley Workshops and STIHL Close relationship A special form of co-operation has linked the Remstal Workshops of the Social Welfare Organisation in Stetten and the STIHL company for more than 20 years. It began with small assembly and disassembly procedures. In the course of time, the task of packing a number of different toolkits was added. STIHL adapted the procedures so that they could be accomplished easily and faultlessly by people with a disability. But this close relationship between the two companies exists beyond that co-operation: Selina Stihl, who is a member of the STIHL advisory and supervisory boards, will join the Welfare Organisation's administrative board as an honorary member in July 2018. It's not all that it seems The touring exhibition "Good Looks. No Substance" informs consumers about the dangers of counterfeit products for people, society and the economy. It is organized by the Aktionskreis gegen Produkt- und Markenpiraterie e.V. (Anti Product Piracy Association) (APM). In Germany alone, the damage caused annually by product and brand piracy amounts to an estimated 50 billion euros. This initially affects companies – but it ultimately results in a loss of jobs and tax revenue. However, the counterfeits present an even greater risk to consumers: It is no longer just luxury watches or handbags that are being forged, but also pharmaceuticals, foods and technical equipment, such as STIHL chainsaws. Outwardly, the illegal copies can be hardly distinguished from the originals, but are of a poorer quality and finish and, at worst, can jeopardize the health and safety of the user. The aim of this APM project is to inform consumers and create an awareness of the dangers of product and brand piracy. STIHL supports the exhibition which has been seen at more than 60 shopping centers so far. Formula 1 in Schools Tomorrow's engineers In the multidisciplinary and international "Formula 1 in Schools" technology competition teams of students design and build a miniature F1 racing car, which they then put through its paces on the racetrack. The teams compete against each other at regional contests and the German championships. Judging includes not just sheer vehicle speed, but also the design, manufacture, reaction time, business plan and a presentation. The aim is to inspire young people to take up technical and engineering careers. STIHL has been sponsoring a regional team since 2012 with donations, know-how and materials. In 2014, the team qualified for the World Finals in Singapore with an outstanding performance at the German championships.

Nachhaltigkeit › Governance Berichterstattung Grundlagen der Berichterstattung Im Jahr 2009 veröffentlichte die Vaillant Group erstmalig einen Nachhaltigkeitsbericht. Seitdem erscheint er einmal pro Jahr und ergänzt unseren ebenfalls jährlich erscheinenden Jahresbericht um wesentliche Aspekte und Kennzahlen in den strategischen Fokusfeldern Umwelt, Mitarbeiter, Entwicklung & Produkte sowie Gesellschaft dar. Die Berichtsinhalte bilden konzernweit Erfolge und Herausforderungen im Bereich Nachhaltigkeit ab und zeigen so einen repräsentativen Querschnitt durch das gesamte Unternehmen. Berichtsrahmen und Datenerhebung Ziel der Berichterstattung ist es, Kunden, Mitarbeitern, Gesellschaftern, Lieferanten, Medienvertretern und weiteren interessierten Stakeholdern einen transparenten Einblick in unsere wichtigsten Werte und in unser Verständnis von nachhaltigem Wirtschaften zu gewähren. Alle produktionsrelevanten Kennzahlen, die wir im Rahmen der Berichterstattung anführen, beziehen sich auf die Vaillant Group Produktionsstätten in sechs europäischen Ländern und China. Die Kennzahlen werden in Form einer zentral gesteuerten schriftlichen Abfrage in den Hauptstandorten erhoben. Bei der Ausweisung der Kennzahlen ist zu beachten, dass es sich sowohl um absolute als auch um relative Zahlen handelt. Dadurch berücksichtigen wir beeinflussende Faktoren, z. B. die Ausweitung von Produktionskapazitäten. Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Seit 2011 orientieren wir uns bei der Berichterstattung der gruppenweiten Nachhaltigkeitsleistung an den international anerkannten Standards der Global Reporting Initiative ( www.globalreporting.org ). Der Anwendungsgrad der GRI-G3-Richtlinien im Rahmen des Nachhaltigkeitsberichts 2012 entspricht gemäß unserer Selbsteinschätzung dem Level „B“. Eine externe Prüfung der Berichterstattung der Vaillant Group gemäß GRI ist weder erfolgt noch geplant. Nachhaltigkeit › Governance Prozesse Nachhaltigkeit in den Prozessen der Vaillant Group Das Handeln innerhalb der Vaillant Group wird von klar definierten Prozessen gesteuert. Diese stellen sicher, dass Nachhaltigkeit in sämtlichen Dimensionen von Beginn an im Unternehmen, in seinen Produkten und in seinen Arbeitsprozessen implementiert wird. Nachhaltigkeit ist in diesen Prozessen fest verankert. Gruppenweit verbindliche Standards Prozessmanagement – das klingt nach kleinlichen Vorschriften, Arbeitsanweisungen und wie das Gegenteil von Kreativität. Doch gerade durch ihre Prozesse sichert die Vaillant Group Nachhaltigkeit über den gesamten Produktlebenszyklus ab. Prozesse steuern das Zusammenspiel zahlreicher Kollegen über Abteilungs- und Ländergrenzen hinweg – und sorgen für gruppeneinheitliche Nachhaltigkeitsstandards. Das beginnt bei der Produktentwicklung und endet erst mit der Produktentsorgung. Umfassende Zertifizierung In diesem Zusammenhang kommt auch der Zertifizierung nach anerkannten Normen eine herausragende Bedeutung. Die gruppenweite Anwendung und Durchsetzung ihrer Qualitäts- und Umweltstandards lässt die Vaillant Group im Rahmen einer sogenannten Multi-Site-Zertifizierung regelmäßig von einem unabhängigen Prüfinstitut testieren. Bislang sind die Standorte Belper (UK), Nantes (F), Remscheid (D), Skalica (SK), Trenčín (SK), Vitoria (ES) und Wuxi (CN) Teil der Vaillant Group Multi-Site-Zertifizierung. In den kommenden Jahren werden sämtliche Produktionsstätten Teil der Multi-Site-Zertifizierung sein. S . Nachhaltigkeit › Strategie Fokusfelder Die Nachhaltigkeitsaktivitäten der Vaillant Group sind in vier Fokusfelder gebündelt: Umwelt, Mitarbeiter, Entwicklung & Produkte sowie Gesellschaft. Das macht unsere Arbeit nicht nur effektiver und transparenter. Auch Erfolge und Herausforderungen bei der steten Verbesserung unserer Nachhaltigkeitsleistung lassen sich so besser nachvollziehen. Durch Klick auf die einzelnen Segmente der Grafik gelangen Sie zu weiteren Informationen. Unsere Ziele Umwelt Der Schutz von Umwelt und Ressourcen ist wichtiger Bestandteil der Vaillant Group Nachhaltigkeitsstrategie. Wir wollen verantwortungsvoll mit Ressourcen umgehen, die CO 2 -Emissionen konsequent senken, negative Einflüsse auf die Umwelt vermeiden und aktiv Chancen nutzen, die Umwelt zu schützen. Mitarbeiter Unsere Mitarbeiter bilden das Fundament und die Seele der Vaillant Group. Die Vaillant Group verfolgt das Ziel, bei Bewerbern und Mitarbeitern der Arbeitgeber der Wahl zu sein. Entwicklung und Produkte Unser Ziel ist es, unseren Kunden energieeffiziente Produkte über den gesamten Produktlebenszyklus hinweg anzubieten – von der Entwicklung über Einkauf, Produktion und Gebrauch bis hin zu Service und Recycling. Gesellschaft Die Vaillant Group bekennt sich zu ihrer gesellschaftlichen Verantwortung. Das Unternehmen engagiert sich dort, wo es unternehmerisch tätig ist, für gesellschaftlichen Fortschritt und das Wohlergehen der Mitmenschen. S . Protecting nature’s resources. And those of our customers. Genia Hybrid is especially efficient when it comes to heating and cooling homes – and consumes much less primary energy than conventional technologies. Because it also saves space, the hybrid system is particularly popular among people with small homes. Extraordinarily economical – and astoundingly easy to install Many people would associate the word “hybrid” with an environmentally friendly drive concept for vehicles. However, the same technology has long since been increasing environmental protection in the field of heating and air-conditioning technology. The hybrid system Genia Hybrid from AWB combines an air-water heat pump with a condensing boiler. The heat pump is particularly efficient when it comes to generating hot water in summer, when the air temperature is high. In winter, the economical condensing boiler keeps the home snug. Genia Hybrid therefore consumes an average of 35 per cent less primary energy, reduces CO₂ emissions by 35 per cent and saves 25 per cent of heating costs compared with conventional systems. These impressive figures mainly come down to the optimally adjusted interaction of system components: the integrated ExaMaster microcomputer coordinates the individual devices based on the energy efficiency being recalculated every minute – therefore determining the best operational mode at any given time. The fact that Genia Hybrid now spares resources and lowers costs in many homes is not least because of an additional benefit attributed to the system, which may not seem all that impressive at first glance: it is particularly easy to install. The majority of blind holes and holes drilled into houses and buildings are no longer needed, neither are complicated connections to existing systems and fittings. Thanks to the minimal effort required for installation and its excellent value for money, using Genia Hybrid in large-scale housing developments is also paying off – installing the device into numerous homes at once makes its advantages even more obvious. Using the following example taken from the Netherlands, the home of our AWB brand, we will show you how the attractive features of the hybrid system make an impact in practice. The advantages of Genia Hybrid open doors. Or better put: open doors to new homes. Low installation time, great value for money: Genia Hybrid gives installers convincing arguments for using the system in large-scale renovation and new build projects. –35% energy consumption –25% heating costs CO₂ emissions It is so simple. Almost like Plug&Play.; When applied to the Genia Hybrid system, the somewhat overused idiom “less is more” takes on a whole new meaning. Thanks to Genia Hybrid, increasing energy efficiency was a piece of cake for Leeuwarden Location: Leeuwarden, Friesland province, the Netherlands. Project: new build comprising 88 flats, Bilgaard residential and commercial centre. Task: to install the hybrid system Genia Hybrid. Sander van der Wagen, project manager at a big Dutch construction company, was astounded by the rapid development his colleague was making in the installation of the Genia Hybrid systems. The expert could see that the installation was running extremely smoothly – much to the joy of his colleague, who was whistling along to his seasoned hand movements. Sander looked on amazed: “It’s so simple. Almost like Plug&Play;!” New experiences with a new kind of technology A new experience for Sander. Many heating systems are extremely complicated – also when it comes to their installation. They can push technicians’ nerves to the limit and costs through the roof. Not to mention the fact that the technology normally takes up a huge amount of space. Economical – but how?! When planning the Bilgaarden project – a shopping centre with integrated living spaces – the Dutch city of Leeuwarden and the building contractor had a joint goal in mind: a heating system was to supply the 88 flats with heat and hot water. But there was not a great deal of time in which to realise the project. To complicate matters, there was only a limited amount of space. The system could only be built into the storage cupboards in the small flats – a space that the occupants desperately needed for a washing machine. Genia Hybrid impresses city and building contractors The ideal solution was soon found in the AWB Genia Hybrid. The hybrid system was selected for its quick and easy installation and the fact that it only takes up 0.1 m³ of space in the flat. The condensing boiler even leaves enough space for a washing machine. The system’s second principal component – the Genia Air air-water heat pump – is housed outside the flats, for example on the roof, as is the case in Leeuwarden. Key system components: the savings box The heating installer suddenly stopped his whistling “What, finished already?” asked Sander van der Wagen. “Not quite. I still need to install one last part.” The technician presented a small device to Sander as if it were a gift. “Do you know what this is?” Sander knew full well that the man was holding an ExaMaster in his hands: the microcomputer calculates the energy efficiency of the system on a minute-by-minute basis and uses this information to decide which component should generate heat and hot water or cool the flat. “Of course I know. That’s the savings box.” Now it was the technician’s turn to look surprised. “It’s simple: because the box is so good at maths, the occupants save 25 per cent of their heating costs. And what do they do with their money?” The workman shrugged his shoulders clueless. “They go and spend it downstairs in the shopping centre, of course!” Genia Hybrid makes Leeuwarden more energy efficient – and happier! A long-term study carried out by the Noorder Hogeschool Leeuwarden shows that Genia Hybrid receives top marks from the inhabitants of Bilgaard residential and commercial centre because the self-adjusting system is easy to use, convenient and extremely economical. Its reliability is another advantage: since the hybrid system was installed in 2010, none of the systems have had a single technical problem or breakdown. This avoids any inconvenience on the part of the occupants and saves maintenance and repair costs on the part of the property managers. Saving energy before it is even installed Manufactured in state-of-the-art facilities in Belper, UK, Glow-worm’s Ultracom² is produced with the environment in mind. The device uses sustainable methods and incorporates parts which allow effective recycling at the end of the product life cycle: a green approach which does not stop at our customers’ doors thanks to easy installation and simple operation. Efficient and sustainable, even during production Ultracom² is a quiet, reliable and efficient solution, which meets the hot water and heating demands of over 500,000 customers in the UK, day and night. The fact that Glow-worm’s Ultracom² is extremely reliable, simple and easy to use and hugely economical has led to it becoming such a popular heating appliance in the demanding UK market. Compared with traditional heaters, Ultracom² consumes 30 per cent less natural gas while also reducing emissions by 30 per cent. This protects the environment and notably reduces heating costs. Glow-worm achieves this impressive level of efficiency by combining a range of high-quality components. The Ultracom² reuses the heat that would normally be released into the atmosphere by traditional heating units. Ultracom² is not only efficient and economical during its operation in the home; the production process in the Belper plant is also very sustainable. How is that possible? Find out more. The goal: achieve less It is fantastic that Ultracom² supplies heating and hot water using such little energy – while being so remarkably easy to use. It is also important that the Ultracom² is manufactured in a sustainable way, helping protect the environment right from the beginning. This would not be possible without the dedication of our employees in the Vaillant Group plant in Belper. –31% CO₂ emissions per appliance produced –61% water consumption –100% landfill waste Taking on responsibility from head to toe What does a customer’s footwear have to do with a heater’s ecological footprint? A great deal! Our UK team shows a huge amount of dedication – and a great deal of tact You may wonder what the shoes worn by an important Glow-worm visitor have to do with a heating unit’s ecological footprint? A great deal. Everything, even. But let’s take one thing at a time! Oxford shoes vs. safety boots One day, when an important visitor arrived at the UK plant in Belper, the team were fully prepared for his visit. However it took a little longer than expected for our guest to make it past the door into the plant, but for good reason. It was immediately clear to a production worker that the Oxford shoes worn by the visitor did not comply with the plant’s safety requirements and so he had to wait a little while until a pair of suitable safety boots could be sent to reception. Zero-tolerance responsibility This little anecdote relates to a much greater topic: responsibility. Every employee at the Vaillant Group’s plant in Belper is and feels responsible for their actions. Everyone is committed to achieving the sustainability goals set by the Vaillant Group. This includes a zero-tolerance attitude to implementing safety procedures. The aim is to significantly reduce the number of work-related accidents as well as meeting the high demands on production in order to save resources, avoid waste and keep emissions to a minimum. Zero landfill: fully committed to zero This commitment is paying off. In 2012 the UK plant had managed to reduce CO₂ emissions by 31 per cent, energy consumption by 35 per cent, water use by 56 per cent and waste volume by 53 per cent compared with 2010 levels – despite increasing production volumes. And that’s not all. Since 2011, the Belper plant has met its zero landfill target – absolutely no waste is sent to landfill. To top this off, a 61 per cent reduction in water consumption per unit was achieved from 2010 to 2013. Belper: the most sustainable production site in the UK In recognition of these achievements, in January 2014 the plant was presented the National EEF/ENER-G Sustainable Manufacturing Award 2013 and named the UK’s most sustainable production site. The award acknowledges the work of the entire team in Belper. This means that when our UK customers opt for the Ultracom², they not only save energy and money with a device that can be used totally intuitively, but it has already done its bit to protect the environment during production, thus minimising the ecological footprint of the Ultracom². The Belper plant has reduced water consumption per unit produced by 61 per cent – a saving of 1 million litres, made possible by changing the test units from water to air pressure and by reusing water in production processes. Zero landfill: the Belper plant does not send anything to landfill. In 2006, 326 tonnes of waste was created by 350,000 appliances produced. A waste-avoidance and recycling scheme has reduced this figure to zero. The CO₂ emissions per appliance produced fell by 31 per cent from 2010 to 2012. This success was made possible thanks to the consistent implementation of energy saving measures and the introduction of more efficient production methods. Slovakian babies love tigers In Slovakia, it is not uncommon for a tiger to be involved in family planning. At the end of the day, parents want to make sure their children are looked after with a reliable heat source that will keep them snug from day one. Efficient, reliable and straight-forward: the Protherm Tiger condensing boiler Many people in Slovakia and other European countries do not necessarily associate the word tiger with an elegant big cat, but with a warm and cosy home – more specifically, with a heater that is easy to use and can be relied upon to provide families with comforting warmth and hot water over long winters. The Protherm Tiger is a wall-hung, gas-fired boiler which utilises natural gas up to the maximum physical limit. Even the residual heat contained in the exhaust gas, which is normally lost through the chimney, serves to provide warmth. The Protherm Tiger uses up to 15 per cent less natural gas than older devices. The appliance is now a bestseller, and not just because of it being so economical: as is the case with all Protherm products, the Tiger is particularly reliable and easy to use. Its dependability and efficiency is put down to the new electronic gas regulation feature, which allows the appliance to always run on the lowest setting necessary. The Tiger is always easy to operate thanks to the “one key – one function” principle. Different desired temperatures can be easily preset for various times throughout the day, making our customers’ lives easier and more comfortable. Efficient, reliable and straight-forward: with these benefits, the Protherm Tiger meets the country-specific requirements in Slovakia and other European markets. The Protherm brand, as part of the Vaillant Group, is therefore able to adjust to the local needs of target groups, while at the same time protecting the environment. Would you have ever imagined so many tigers being fixed members of the family? In many homes across Europe, the Protherm Tiger is a beloved member of the family – the figures speak for themselves: Protherm ranks among the Vaillant Group’s family of brands with eight international heating technology brands. 1 warm and comfortable home tiger baby The Bielik family from Bratislava are expecting a baby. And a tiger! “We can depend on a Protherm Tiger to deliver reliable warmth for our baby; the same can’t be said of the antique currently hanging on our wall.” The baby finds its place in the world; the Tiger finds its place on the wall! Adriana strokes her round tummy with pride. “Just three months to go. Or maybe three and a half if the little one is feeling especially comfortable in mummy’s tummy.” Adriana, 27 years old, and her husband Branislav, 28 years old, have known each other since their school days – the couple have been inseparable for ten years. Family planning: for many years this was not something the couple thought about. They first focussed on finishing their studies and successfully finding their feet on the career ladder. However, ever since getting married and moving into their first home three years ago, Adriana and Branislav realised that there was something missing from their lives: children. “We have been talking about children from a rather practical perspective for a while now,” says Branislav. “At some point we realised that our conversations had gained a real sense of longing.” – “It was more than just a passing phase, clearly!” adds the soon-to-be mum. Branislav opens the door to the bathroom. His facial expression changes from cheerful to glum as he points to an oversized grey cylinder on the wall. That’s what we currently use to heat our home. It’s already over twenty years old. It uses a huge amount of gas. – But what’s worse is that it’s constantly breaking down. In winter it’s uncomfortable for us as the flat is often freezing without the heater. But for a baby it would be downright dangerous. It is no wonder the young couple made the decision to buy a Tiger a while ago – the Protherm gas-fired boiler is particularly energy-efficient and completely reliable. Arranging an installation date for the Tiger was easy: it will move into the flat before the birth and will make sure that the family are warm and cosy from day one. A development engineer at his workplace in Skalica, Slovakia: this is where the Protherm teams planned the use of the hydraulic block. Installation of a Protherm Tiger, which incorporates the condensing heat exchanger. This part makes a huge contribution to the high reliability of the gas-fired boiler due to its condensation process, which allows the heat exchanger to absorb the latent heat in these combustion gases and use it to preheat the cooler water returning from the heating circuit. Quality inspection of the appliance: following controls and various hours of testing, it receives the well-deserved certification: all tests passed! Now it’s time for the Protherm Tiger to go on sale – it will not be long before it is being depended on to warm up a home in Slovakia or another country around the world. Mini electronics for maxi efficiency Electronics for the electric wall-hung heater: the Protherm Ray is controlled by microprocessors, which also ensure that the appliance always supplies heat and hot water as efficiently as possible. The control panel with its integrated display allows intuitive, easy operation. Saving is a given The wireless regulator system Thermolink RC regulates heat and hot water based on programs which adjust themselves to the time of the day and individual preferences, thus reducing energy consumption and lowering heating costs. Down to earth in every meaning of the phrase The Protherm Panther Condens with its integrated turbo system represents quality and environmentally friendly economy thanks to an impressive efficiency factor of up to 108 per cent. Its excellent value for money appeals to an increasing number of customers. The grease is removed from the tubes One important part of the tube production process in Remscheid is an industrial cleaning system. The tubes are transported into the system in baskets. The giant washing machine removes all traces of oil, grease and metal swarf from the copper and steel parts at a temperature of 70 °C. The sun also plays its part The modularly structured washing machine can be adapted to the number of tubes to be cleaned – saving a great deal of energy and water. A separate bath for better results Once the cleaning programme is complete, the washing machine pumps away the foamy rinse water. The basket with the freshly washed tubes comes back out of the system automatically. The shiny components are now optimally prepared for the next production steps. Press release Remscheid, 26 January 2016 International study: Germany is only average in green ranking Study on sustainable attitudes and everyday habits surveyed people in 13 countries Germany came out seventh in the international ranking Significant room for improvement regarding energy consumption and consumer behaviour Germans are champions when it comes to avoiding plastic bags, saving water and separating rubbish. This was revealed by an international study conducted by Vaillant, in cooperation with the market research institute TNS Infratest. A total of 13,500 people from 13 countries were asked about their eco-friendly behaviour for the study. The respondents’ green intelligence quotient, or “green IQ”, was calculated on the basis of more than 100 questions concerning mobility, shopping habits, and energy-use and heating habits, among other things. “As a provider of energy-saving heating technology, we wanted to know how green people’s everyday habits really are, and what differences there are between countries,” says Dr Andree Groos, Managing Director for Vaillant Group Sales, Marketing and Service. “In addition, we wanted to raise awareness of the topic of sustainability and show that every one of us can contribute to protecting the environment and saving resources.” German is seventh in the international ranking. Turkey and Austria top the list, while Poland comes last. The full results of the study and a test for calculating your own green IQ can be accessed at www.mygreenIQ.com . A mixed bag of results for Germany Germans are the most conscientious nation at avoiding plastic bags, with 82 per cent of people in this country using reusable baskets or bags to carry their grocery shopping. That is a higher rate than in any other country. Germans are also leaders when it comes to conserving water, according to the study. The majority (83 per cent) turn off the tap while cleaning their teeth. And Germans are also exemplary when it comes to separating their rubbish: almost 85 per cent do so, a rate beaten only by the Belgians. On the other hand, just 19 per cent of Germans know what the energy consumption level of their home is. And consumer behaviour in Germany also leaves a lot be desired: just nine per cent of respondents said they would be prepared to pay more for products with a fair trade label. Another interesting result from the study is that women generally have a higher green IQ than men do. Although German men seem to have a more eco-friendly attitude, the country’s women are streets ahead in terms of actual behaviour. About the study Sustainability is one of the most frequently used buzzwords of our time. Nowadays everything is required to be as environmentally friendly as possible, from bananas, to holidays, to jeans, to cars. But how do people in eastern, western, northern and southern Europe really think and behave? How much energy do they consume, what are their shopping habits and what mobility options do they use? The heating technology specialist Vaillant and the market research institute TNS Infratest surveyed 13,500 people in 13 countries. The full results of the study and a test for calculating your own green IQ can be accessed at About Vaillant Vaillant offers its customers worldwide eco-friendly, energy-saving heating and ventilation systems that make increasing use of renewable energies. Its product portfolio encompasses solar-thermal and photovoltaic systems, heat pumps, pellet boilers, ventilation systems for low-energy buildings, combined heat and power stations, high-efficiency heating systems using fossil fuels, and intelligent controls. All aboard and accounted for: a highly efficient system solution from Vaillant. Manfred Ceplecha from the Vaillant Group Austria is happy to show you around. Sustainable energy supply for a visionary project: full speed ahead for Noah’s Ark Manfred Ceplecha from the Vaillant Group Austria is proud of the system configuration in the building services room: “Projects like this help us demonstrate the technical potential of an ecological and energy-related heating revolution.” Every resident contributes towards the community It goes without saying that the Noah’s Ark community in Imst, Tyrol, uses renewable energy sources: the unusual building project nestled within the Austrian Alps achieves sustainable goals across all areas of everyday living and cohabitation. The heating technology used in the building complex thus comes from Vaillant. The green brand of the Vaillant Group’s family of brands has supplied a system solution which is anything but ordinary – and which fulfils the ambitious demands of Noah’s Ark. The project is strongly perceived among the general public. The topic has even been addressed on several occasions by the media. Noah’s Ark in Imst is much more than a simple housing development. The residents do not lead anonymous lives next door to each other. Instead, they support each other within a vibrant community which spans many generations and social strata. The cooperation benefits from the contribution made by each individual – social points are awarded to residents for services they perform within the community. The Vaillant system solution is ideally integrated into the living concept The building complex, which takes the form of a ship, has 18 housing units with outdoor facilities and a shared wing, which also incorporates a bakery and spa area – as well as a communal recreation room, the centre of the community’s social life. Barely a peep can be heard from the building services room: despite not hearing it, the equipment does its bit to aid communal living – working in a highly efficient yet still particularly sustainable manner. Manfred Ceplecha points to the devices: Noah’s Ark has given us the opportunity to demonstrate the strengths of our brand as a one-stop supplier. The main challenge was to optimally network the components into an overall system so as to achieve the highest possible level of energy efficiency. Determining the right control sequence was essential in prioritising the renewable energy sources. Cooperating for greater sustainability The parallel operation of geothermal heat pump, solar system and two CHP units is unusual – the latter generate electricity which operates the heat pump and provide the swimming pool with warm water. Surplus electricity is fed into the national grid. The system is rounded off with a ventilation system, condensing technology and several storage units. “I think the Noah’s Ark concept is wonderful. It would be great if other people copied the idea,” says Manfred Ceplecha summing up. Just a few moments later the sound of his footsteps fades away; only the quiet hum of the equipment remains. Engineers and project managers working for our Vaillant brand analyse the energy requirement of the building complex on site and review the possibilities of installing a heating and electricity system which is both sustainable and efficient. Back at the office in Vienna, the team works on the ideal system solution. Many questions are yet to be answered: which components should be used? How is the network best structured? What would be the best control sequence? The specialists from Vienna are on site while the integrated system is assembled and installed. Working hand in hand with the contractor, the sophisticated configuration begins to take shape. It is not long before the system is making a contribution towards even greater sustainability. In the case of a high energy requirement, the ecoPOWER 4.7 unleashes its benefits in the form of a cascade connection or as part of an integrated system. Extra large, extra efficient: extraordinary!
